extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and agents
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing how examiners should handle deferrals/extensions, document service, personal interviews, amendments (especially in response to final rejection), and decisions to grant or reject patent applications within KIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review frequency for deferred/extended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application whose examination or processing has been already deferred or extended respectively, an examiner shall review more than one time a month to confirm whether the reasons causing deferral or extension have been resolved or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the review confirms all reasons for examination deferral or extension of processing period have been cleared up, an examiner shall conduct the examination by the termination date of the extension of examination deferral or processing period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-extension/deferral reporting and time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the examiner considers the examination to be deferred and the processing period to be extended again because the application does not overcome the previous deferral or extension reason or new reasons occur, it shall be reported to the head of the examination division (team) following a head of the examination unit, and the deferral or extension shall be made within two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: if deferral/extension is due to causes not imputable to the examiner (e.g., outsourced prior art search report not delivered, copies of prior art not yet secured), further extension may be allowed under those grounds (④ and ⑥ among grounds referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on extensions when causes imputable vs not imputable to examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: Further extension of deferral/processing period can be extended again only in the case of causes not imputable to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of reasons not imputable to the examiner include where the prior art search report has not been delivered or where copies of the prior art literature are requested to external institutions but have not been secured yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of reasons for renewed deferral/extension
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner once again decides to defer the examination or extend the processing period according to the abovementioned case, he/she notifies the applicant specific reasons of deferral or extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent trial/proceeding as grounds for deferral
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent trial or proceeding related to the application concerned being pending (including administrative trial or litigation on the application procedure) is a ground for examination deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of later-filed applications on identical invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Where more than two patent applications are filed on the identical invention, the examiner shall defer examination for later-filed applications until the prior-filed application has been processed or has been laid-open or registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where the later-filed application can be rejected based on the same ground as the ground for rejection for the prior-filed application, the examiner can start examination. Detailed methods vary based on identicalness of applicants and disclosure status of the prior-filed application (table specifying actions: e.g., examination conducted and Article 36(1) ground notified, or examination deferred until disclosure of prior-filed application).

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting examination on later-filed application after prior-filed processed
rubrics_metrics.description: When the prior-filed application is examined or laid open or registered after examination on later-filed applications is deferred, the examiner may conduct examination on the later-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even though examination on later-filed application is conducted, the examiner shall make the final decision on examination in applying Article 36(1) of the Patent Act once the scope of claim of the prior-filed application is determined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document service general principle — registered mail
rubrics_metrics.description: The documents shall be served by registered mail except for the cases where the party or his/her agent receives in person or uses information network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of sending documents by post mail, the registration receipt shall be kept. Note: trial rulings or written decisions regarding patent trials, retrials, or cancellations shall be served by a special service method according to postal service laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service to legitimate receiver (agent rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents shall be served to a legitimate receiver, referring to an agent if appointed, sub-agent or agent appointed midway except for special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of two or more agencies, except for special cases, the legitimate receiver shall be the agent described first in a written patent application. For multiple agents with general power, serve preferentially to the agent having been appointed for the relevant case. If receiver is incompetent, serve legal representative. For multiple applicants, serve representative if elected or the applicant stated first in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service address and change notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of documents shall be made to residential or business address of an entitled receiver unless reporting other address for service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change of service address shall be reported without delay. Note: where failure of service is due to rejection by a receiver without justifiable reason, the date of sending is regarded as a receiving date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by public notification when address unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: When documents cannot be served because the residential or business address of the addressee is unclear (unable to verify even using the Resident Registration Use System), the documents shall be served by public notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cases where two or more persons go through patent procedure and all their addresses cannot be verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure before resorting to public notification — step ①
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents are returned, an officer shall file facts regarding the document returns (return number, reason) to a computer system and communicate to an examiner in charge. The examiner shall verify the address of a legitimate receiver by telephone and resend the returned documents with the 'Guide to Report on Information Change in Applicant' and form to report change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for public notification when phone and resident system agree — step ②
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the telephone verification step, where the address confirmed by the Resident Registration Use System is identical with the address confirmed by telephone, an examiner shall serve documents by public notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not identical, an examiner shall serve again the documents to the address confirmed by the Resident Registration Use System according to the telephone-confirmation procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for repeated returns — step ③
rubrics_metrics.description: Where documents were sent again to the address confirmed through the Resident Registration Use System but returned again, documents shall be served by public notification with no further procedure for address confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation address exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a receiver is a corporation, the Resident Registration Use System cannot be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, an examiner shall exert most available efforts to confirm a correct address of a corporation and send documents to a legal address at least once before public notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in document service methods
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may adopt a different service method where, through case-by-case review, an examiner finds a new service method for sure sending to a legitimate receiver.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service shall otherwise be made according to the Rules on Office Management and Patent Net System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization for personal interview
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant or his/her agent requests or where an examiner considers necessary for a prompt and fair examination, an examiner may have a personal interview with the party as an ancillary method for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases requiring a personal interview include: comparative explanation between claimed invention and prior art; clarification of the ground for rejection; explanation of a written argument; subject matter complicated/sophisticated; or other cases where examiner recognizes need.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request a personal interview and timing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The party requests a personal interview by fax, telephone, information network (including e-mail), or written application in person. If multiple applications, file individually for each unless same examiner, then one request for all is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request may be filed after examination begins but not later than the decision to grant a patent. For an application decided to be rejected, the party may request an interview until an appeal trial against the decision is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner-initiated interview and scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may request and set a date for an interview in writing, by fax or telephone, only when telephone discussion is not sufficient to reconcile ideas between examiner and applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates may change by agreement and change must be included in the personal interview log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner response standards to interview requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the party requests a personal interview, an examiner should respond actively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the request is plain business contact, questions about examination progress, general patentability questions, repeated requests for same application, or unrelated issues, the examiner may ask the party to modify the request or disregard it. When communicating about an interview (phone/fax/email), the examiner shall include dates and persons in communications, due date and form of the interview, and a contact number in the examination report in the Patent Examination Processing System.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview procedure and modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: A personal interview is face-to-face in principle; meeting rooms at the patent customer service center are preferred. Video phone interviews may use designated video conference rooms (e.g., Multimedia Center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For face-to-face interviews, the meeting room at patent customer service center is principle; remote video facilities may be used as listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner preparation for interview
rubrics_metrics.description: For a personal interview to be more smooth and effective, an examiner shall in advance review relevant documents and print them if necessary. If prior contact confirms a discussion topic, examiner shall organize related issues in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If necessary, an examiner may request the party provide reference documents or multimedia related to prior art in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate interviewee and proxy requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Before an interview, an examiner shall confirm whether a participant is a legitimate interviewee: applicant (or representative if corporation), agent of the application, or a person with evidential statement showing legitimate entrustee appointed by an agent/applicant (sub-agent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A participant with delegation limited to a personal interview shall submit a proxy statement at every interview, but may combine delegations for multiple interviews into one proxy statement by listing application numbers. A legitimate interviewee may be accompanied by an inventor or related person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview log content and sealing
rubrics_metrics.description: In the interview log, an examiner shall state an application number, name of an examiner and participants, and contents and result of interview. The interview log, sealed with signatures of an examiner and participants, shall be submitted to an officer in charge at the patent customer service center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contents of an interview shall be included in the examination report of the Patent Examination Processing System. When exchanging opinions on restricted issues, the examiner shall briefly state the exchanged opinion in the interview log.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview conduct rules and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall proceed swiftly on a basis of personal interviews and any agreements made shall be conducted within the shortest time possible. A personal interview shall not be a basis for an examiner to simplify or omit requisite statements in notifications or written decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new ground for rejection is discovered after interview, examiner shall communicate the purport to the party and continue examination. Examiner may request party to submit materials presented at interview. Principle is one interview per application; if necessary, up to two times. If interview occurs within period for submission of written argument, participant must submit responding documents per agreement; if applicant responds differently, must communicate to examiner. Interview is not basis for applicant to simplify/omit requisite statements in written argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview on visit rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request an examiner to visit for communication (personal interview on visit). Examiner contacts by telephone to determine need; such visits are allowed only if telephone communication is difficult or if necessary for prompt and accurate examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal interview on visit is in principle carried out in a Regional Intellectual Property Center; may be elsewhere by mutual agreement. Procedures follow general personal interview rules, including logging and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner determination whether to refuse to enter amendments after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike non-final rejection, when receiving an amendment in response to notice of final grounds for rejection necessitated by amendment, an examiner shall determine whether to refuse to enter the amendment before assessing patentability and confirm matters to be examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting the written argument, an applicant may argue that the notice of final rejection necessitated by amendment is inappropriate; examiner shall review appropriateness considering applicant's assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness review for 'final rejection necessitated by amendment'
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether issuance of the final rejection necessitated by amendment is appropriate shall be referred to the types of notice of grounds for rejection. Where issuance is deemed appropriate, examiner shall review whether amendment requirements are satisfied. Where deemed inappropriate, examiner shall admit the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action when final-rejection-necessitated amendment not overcome or absent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the grounds indicated in the final rejection necessitated by amendment are not overcome, the examiner will take proper actions: (①) where no amendment is made or amendment limited to response to final rejection necessitated by amendment, examiner shall notify grounds for rejection again instead of making decision to reject; the type of ground is decided by referral to types of notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (②) where applicant treats the final rejection as non-final and submits amendment in response to non-final rejection, examiner shall make decision to reject. Examples illustrate admissions/refusals depending on whether amendment generates new grounds for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to enter amendment when amendment generates new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment in response to final rejection fails to meet amendment scope prescribed in Article 47(2) and (3), or where new grounds for rejection occur from the amendment (excluding certain deletions), the amendment shall be refused to be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new ground of rejection can be cured by ex-officio amendment, the examiner shall approve the amendment and carry out subsequent procedures. New ground does not include grounds that were previously notified or existed without notification. Several concrete examples (adding/deleting elements or claims) illustrate how to decide admission vs refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order of considering multiple amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant in response to the final notification submits multiple amendments within the designated period, an examiner shall determine whether to admit or refuse to enter the amendments in reverse order of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claim deletions that cause dependent-claim deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment was deletion of claims and subsequently generated a new ground for rejection (e.g., a dependent claim referring only to the deleted claim has deficiency), an examiner shall not refuse to enter the amendment for that reason alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner shall admit the amendment unless there are other reasons for refusal, and then notify the new rejection grounds at the final rejection necessitated by amendment. If deletion leaves the remaining claims understandable excluding the deleted claim, it's a clerical error not a ground for rejection and should be subject to ex officio amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision to refuse to enter amendment must be written and separate
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision to refuse to enter amendment shall be made in writing separately from the decision to reject an application, specifying reasons why the amendment had to be refused to be entered for the subsequent procedural convenience for an applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant cannot appeal a decision to refuse to enter amendment during substantive examination; it can be dealt with only in the trial against the decision to reject. Certain refusals (e.g., before revocation during ex-officio reexamination) shall not be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination steps after admission of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the amendment is appropriately made, an examiner shall admit the amendment and determine the specification to be examined after reflecting the amendment, followed by actions such as assessment of patentability, notifications and decision to grant or reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grounds for rejection are not overcome by the amendment, make decision to reject; otherwise grant. If notified grounds are overcome but other grounds are generated, notify applicant of new grounds as per types of notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: No retroactive refusal after grant or notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner overlooks that an inappropriate amendment in response to the final rejection was made and then makes a decision to grant a patent or notifies non-final or final grounds, he/she cannot refuse to enter the previous amendment retroactively upon discovery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure after refusal to enter amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: After refusing to enter amendment, an examiner shall continue examining the pre-amended specification. If, upon review, the final rejection necessitated by amendment is not overcome, examiner shall make decision to reject; if the final rejection is inappropriate and no other grounds exist, make decision to grant; if other grounds exist, notify again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and conditions for decision to grant or reject
rubrics_metrics.description: Once completing the examination, an examiner shall make a decision to grant or reject without delay. Where examination of formalities discovers deficiency in application procedure, the final decision shall be made after the procedural deficiency is remedied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and confirmation of decision to grant a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no ground for rejection is discovered, an examiner shall make a decision to grant a patent in writing with rationale attached. The written decision shall include application number, title, name and address of applicant and agent, text of decision and its rationale, number of claims to be patented, date of decision, matters amended ex officio, along with examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commissioner shall deliver a certified copy to the applicant; the decision is confirmed upon delivery. For certain applications (filed by KIPO examiners, recent retirees, or KIPO-supervised prior art searchers), the examiner shall determine consequences in consultation with three persons including a director or head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and confirmation of decision to reject an application
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant fails to overcome grounds for rejection, an examiner shall make a decision to reject in writing with rationale attached. The written decision shall include application number, title, name and address of applicant and agent, date of notice of grounds, text and rationale of decision, and date of decision, with examiner's sign and seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner delivers certified copy; decision is confirmed when it cannot be revoked (e.g., no appeal). If a ground may be cured by ex-officio amendment, examiner shall make ex-officio amendment and allow grant. Examiner shall indicate determination on applicant's amendment and issuable items in the written argument. For applications with multiple claims, if any claim contains grounds for rejection, make decision to reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on unreasonable rationale for rejection and new prior art notice
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner shall not make a decision to reject based on unreasonable rationale other than the already notified ground for rejection, which includes additional request for new documents relating to prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To refer to new prior art, an examiner shall notify that very fact as a ground for rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling third-party submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: When examining an application with information provided by a third party as grounds for rejection, an examiner shall take requisite measures before making final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner shall notify the information provider of his/her decision and whether the provided information is used in the examination when the examination closes, except where the provider lacked capacity or the application is abandoned (further details follow beyond this chunk).
